worked_solution:
If we let $u=\frac{x}{3},$ then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\text{d}u.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {6}^{x/3}\,\text{d}x & =\int {6}^{u}\cdot 3\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {6}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\frac{{6}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}+C \\  & =\frac{3\cdot {6}^{x/3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}+C\end{aligned}
$$
